title: Design System: Irbing Moreno — Interactive CV

body.purpose: Default UI and body copy token; renders via system-ui fallback in the shipped build — Inter itself is never linked.

mono.purpose: Previously a declared-but-unloaded token (Terminal Dev's body renders via ui-monospace fallback). As of this build, Candy Brand actually loads JetBrains Mono 500/700 via its own fontHref and uses it for dates/status/stack-tags.

display.purpose: Named display token, never loaded; Candy Brand's real display face is Baloo 2, loaded independently via its own fontHref.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Shared resting elevation used elsewhere in the build.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Shared hover/raised elevation used elsewhere in the build.

shadows.name: candy-hard-offset-theme-rest
shadows.purpose: Candy Brand card/hero/h1/heading resting shadow — var(--candy-shadow) is lime in dark mode, pure black in light mode (paired with the border, which flips the same way). An earlier version kept this fixed-lime in both themes; changed to theme-paired at explicit user direction.

shadows.name: candy-hard-offset-theme-hover
shadows.purpose: Candy Brand card hover shadow, paired with translate(-3px,-3px); same theme-paired color as the resting shadow.

shadows.name: candy-hard-offset-ink
shadows.purpose: Candy Brand lime-filled chips (badge, solid pill, tags) — shadow renders in ink so the chip doesn't merge into the dark canvas, in both themes. This is a separate device from the theme-paired shadow above; it does not flip.

motion.name: stagger-grid-in
motion.value: gsap.from(items, { opacity:0, scale:0.92, y:16, duration:0.4, stagger:{each:0.06, from:'center', grid:'auto'}, ease:'back.out(1.4)' })
motion.purpose: Bouncy grid entrance, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reveal-on-scroll
motion.value: gsap.from(el, { opacity:0, y:12, duration:0.35, ease:'power1.out', scrollTrigger:{start:'top 90%', toggleActions:'play none none reverse'} })
motion.purpose: Subtle one-at-a-time scroll reveal, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Nav Switcher
components.description: Fixed top bar shared verbatim across every world: design switcher, language toggle, theme toggle.
components.css: .ds-nav { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 16px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; background: color-mix(in srgb, #f7f7f8 85%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); border-bottom: 1px solid #d8d8de; } .ds-nav-designs, .ds-nav-controls { display: flex; gap: 6px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-nav-btn { font-size: 13px; border: 1px solid #ccc; background: #ffffff; color: #16161a; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; line-height: 1; } .ds-nav-btn[aria-current="true"] { background: #d6fa3a; border-color: #d6fa3a; color: #0a0a08; font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-btn:hover { filter: brightness(0.96); } .ds-nav-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #6d5efc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Candy Brand Card
components.description: Neubrutalist outlined card on the near-black canvas, lime hard-offset shadow, used for each resume experience entry.
components.html:
Senior Full Stack Engineer

components.css: .ds-candy-card { background: #141411; border: 3px solid #d6fa3a; border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #d6fa3a; padding: 20px 22px; transition: transform 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease; } .ds-candy-card:hover { transform: translate(-3px, -3px); box-shadow: 9px 9px 0 #d6fa3a; } .ds-candy-card-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; } .ds-candy-card h3 { font-family: 'Baloo 2', sans-serif; margin: 0; font-size: 1.3rem; color: #f4f4ef; } .ds-candy-dates { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 700; color: #d6fa3a; } .ds-candy-desc { color: #b7b7ac; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Candy Brand Pill Button
components.description: Fully rounded CTA pill; ghost variant outlines lime on black, solid variant is a lime chip with ink text/outline — used for the GitHub/LinkedIn/mailto row.
components.html: Email meGitHub
components.css: .ds-candy-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 18px; border-radius: 999px; border: 3px solid #d6fa3a; font-weight: 800; text-decoration: none; color: #f4f4ef; background: #141411; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #d6fa3a; transition: transform 0.15s ease; } .ds-candy-pill:hover { transform: translate(-2px, -2px); } .ds-candy-pill:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #d6fa3a; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-candy-pill-solid { background: #d6fa3a; color: #0a0a08; border-color: #0a0a08; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #0a0a08; }

components.name: Candy Brand Chip (badge / stack-tags)
components.description: Solid-lime, ink-outlined chip used for the name badge and stack-tags — Candy Brand's bordered-fill treatment for tags and callouts. Headlines are deliberately NOT this component — see Candy Brand Headline.
components.css: .ds-candy-chip { display: inline-block; background: #d6fa3a; color: #0a0a08; font-weight: 800; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 999px; border: 3px solid #0a0a08; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #0a0a08; }

components.name: Candy Brand Headline
components.description: Boxed headline for h1 and section headings (.candy-heading) — the same card device (surface fill, theme-paired outline + hard-offset shadow) as .candy-card/.candy-hero, not a flat/unboxed treatment and not the solid-lime ink-text chip either (both tried and reverted during this build). Matches the reference's 'COMPATIBLE CON OPENAI' badge: a bordered box with bright text on a dark fill. Text color is var(--candy-headline) (off-white on the dark surface, near-ink on the light surface); border/shadow color is var(--candy-outline)/var(--candy-shadow), lime in dark mode and pure black (wider, 4px) in light mode. .candy-heading keeps the confirmed rotate(-1deg) sticker tilt.
components.css: h1 { display: block; width: fit-content; font-family: 'Baloo 2', sans-serif; font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 5vw, 3.2rem); font-weight: 800; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: -0.01em; line-height: 1.15; padding: 10px 24px; color: #f4f4ef; background: #141411; border: 3px solid #d6fa3a; border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #d6fa3a; } .ds-candy-heading { font-family: 'Baloo 2', sans-serif; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 800; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f4f4ef; background: #141411; padding: 6px 18px; border: 3px solid #d6fa3a; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #d6fa3a; transform: rotate(-1deg); } /* Light mode: background #ffffff, color #15150f, border/shadow #000000, border-width 4px. */

components.name: Candy Brand Highlighter Mark
components.description: World-local inline <mark> device: solid lime block behind text with box-decoration-break: clone, used once on the hero job-title line. Not a shared text-emphasis primitive.
components.css: .ds-candy-highlight { background: #d6fa3a; color: #0a0a08; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 4px; box-decoration-break: clone; -webkit-box-decoration-break: clone; }

narrative.northStar: The Same Resume, Three Live Proofs
narrative.overview:
This is not one visual system with variants; it is one shared primitive layer (src/styles/tokens.css) feeding deliberately distinct, simultaneously-shipped visual worlds, each rendered by the framework it claims to prove: Candy Brand (React, neubrutalist "dev-tool landing page" — black canvas, one lime signal color, hard-offset card chrome), Terminal Dev (Lit/Web Components, dark CLI/cyberpunk), and two further worlds rendered under the names Neon and Dotfiles in the shipped nav-switcher. A hiring manager switches between them via the nav-switcher without losing theme or language state. The multiplicity is the product claim (see PRODUCT.md Positioning) — do not collapse it into a single invented house style, and do not promote any one world's devices onto the others.

What is genuinely shared and durable: the token layer (color roles, neutral ramp, radius scale, the two soft shadow tokens, light/dark semantic swap via [data-theme]), the <nav-switcher> Web Component, and the per-world convention — now followed by Candy Brand, Neon, and Dotfiles alike — of setting --color-accent / --color-accent-contrast on <html> on mount so the shared nav-switcher active-button fill and the site-wide scrollbar pick up that world's accent while its page is showing.

What is deliberately not shared: display typography, elevation language (soft vs. hard-offset), and card geometry. Each world's Components entry is normative only within that world.
keyCharacteristics: One token source of truth; three-plus independent expressions on top of it.
Soft, layered elevation is the shared default (--shadow-sm / --shadow-md); Candy Brand's hard-offset shadows are a world-local override, not a system default.
Light/dark is a single [data-theme] attribute swap on :root, consistent across all worlds.

Declared webfont families: Baloo 2, Nunito, and (as of this build) JetBrains Mono are actually fetched by Candy Brand; Inter and Poppins remain named-but-unloaded tokens, rendering via system fallback everywhere in the shipped build.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Light and dark mode are the same neutral ramp read from opposite ends, swapped by a single [data-theme] attribute on :root. No world defines a second, independent dark palette.

rules.name: The World-Scoped Shadow Rule
rules.body: Hard-offset, zero-blur shadows are Candy Brand's device, confirmed by its own neubrutalist reference material. Do not apply them to other worlds, and do not fold them into the shared --shadow-sm/--shadow-md tokens as a system-wide default.

rules.name: The Two-Job Border Rule
rules.body: In Candy Brand, outline and shadow are not the same color. The outline flips with theme to stay legible against its own canvas; the shadow stays the fixed lime accent in both themes. Don't collapse them back into a single theme-locked color when extending this world.

dos: Do read all color, radius, and soft-shadow values from tokens.css custom properties in any new surface — never hardcode a hex that already has a token.
Do keep <nav-switcher> visually identical across every world; it is the one cross-world constant.
Do scope a world's signature device (Candy's lime-on-black hard-offset chrome, highlighter mark, and mono code-chip labels; Terminal's CLI-reveal and local CRT palette) to that world only.

Do, in Candy Brand specifically, keep the outline theme-flipped (lime on dark canvas, ink on light canvas) and the shadow fixed-lime in both themes; this is the confirmed, shipped pairing, not an arbitrary choice to re-derive.
donts: Don't apply Candy Brand's hard-offset, zero-blur shadows or 3px outline borders to other worlds; they read as a different, un-reconciled material system there.

Don't treat Inter/Poppins as confirmed rendered faces when adding new UI — only Baloo 2, Nunito, and (in Candy Brand only) JetBrains Mono are actually loaded; verify a webfont link exists before relying on it.
Don't introduce new icon-only controls using raw emoji glyphs without a text label or aria-label; the nav-switcher's sun/moon toggle is a carried defect, not a pattern to repeat.

Don't reuse Candy Brand's old violet/magenta accent assignment when extending this world; the shared Electric Violet/Hot Magenta tokens are no longer part of its palette, even though they remain valid for other worlds.
